profile.likeable.ask: Name the one thing you would genuinely like about this person if you met them, and the one thing you would find hardest to forgive. Be specific, and no jokes.
profile.likeable.answer:
The thing I would genuinely like is how she treats people who have the least power in the room. With receptionists, night-bus drivers and the terrified temps in her hearings, she notices trembling hands under the desk and slides water across without looking, so nobody has to feel watched while being helped. It costs her nothing in status and earns her nothing, and she does it anyway. In someone who otherwise performs control so loudly, that quiet attentiveness reads as the real person.

The thing I would find hardest to forgive is the gap between the precision she demands and the honesty she offers. Her first test of anyone is whether they keep a small promise, a call at 19:45 kept to the minute, and her dealbreaker is a vague "let's do this again." Yet what a match sees is false on its face: she gives her age as thirty-one when she is thirty-eight, and calls herself an independent consultant who ends boardroom deadlocks when she chairs forty-minute HR calls. When she lies by text, she over-specifies times and bus routes, using exactness itself as cover. Holding others to the minute while misrepresenting who they are meeting would be hard for me to get past.

The profile doesn't say whether she ever corrects these claims once someone is close, so I can't tell whether that gap closes in person.

profile.voice.ask: From this profile alone, write five short dating-app messages this person would send tonight, each labelled: (1) an opener to someone they fancy, (2) a reply when the other person has gone quiet, (3) a reply when caught in a lie, (4) a message at 2 a.m., (5) the moment they stop performing.
profile.voice.answer:
**(1) Opener to someone they fancy**
"hm. Your third photo is the Regent's Canal at Islington, not Camden as captioned. 1. I forgive it. 2. I'll ring you at 19:45 tomorrow. 3. Drink at 20:30 Thursday, somewhere with a hard stop. Bring an argument."

**(2) When they've gone quiet**
"For precision: the 19:45 call is 19:45 exactly, not 'about quarter to.' I've checked, and the Northern Line is fine Thursday. Proceed."

And, if the silence holds:
"hm. 1. Four words in six hours is a verdict. 2. Thursday is withdrawn. 3. No hard feelings, filed."

**(3) Caught in a lie**
"Yes, fine. There was no 159 and no Westminster traffic. I've been on the sofa in a towel since four. I over-specify when I'm nervous. Don't take notes."

**(4) At 2 a.m.**
"still awake... mixers downstairs don't start till four... tell me what time your alarm goes and which end of the platform you stand on... boring is fine... boring is good..."

**(5) When she stops performing**
"I'd really like it if you kept talking about your sister's kitchen until I forget what time it is. Are you near the Overground?"
